We will not use any to the Evaluation Materials for any purpose other than the exclusive purpose of evaluating a Possible Transaction.  

TARGET STATEMENT:
The contract entails that the relevant party must keep confidential the existence, terms, subject matter, or status of the agreement, negotiations, discussions, or transaction between the parties.

Determine whether the contract context entails the target statement.

arguments.text: The contract context lacks an explicit confidentiality clause covering the existence, terms, subject matter, or status of the agreement.
arguments.legal_rule: Contract NLI requires explicit textual support or direct inference for confidentiality obligations; absence of such a clause attacks entailment.
arguments.evidence_span: We will not use any to the Evaluation Materials for any purpose other than the exclusive purpose of evaluating a Possible Transaction.

arguments.text: The provided text only imposes a purpose limitation on the use of Evaluation Materials, which is legally and functionally distinct from a confidentiality obligation regarding the transaction itself.
arguments.legal_rule: Purpose limitations on information use do not automatically create confidentiality duties over the agreement's existence or terms.
arguments.evidence_span: We will not use any to the Evaluation Materials for any purpose other than the exclusive purpose of evaluating a Possible Transaction.

arguments.text: The target statement requires the contract to entail a duty to keep confidential the existence, terms, or status of the agreement, but the narrative is entirely silent on this obligation.
arguments.legal_rule: In contract NLI, silence on a material element of the target claim attacks logical entailment.

arguments.text: No definitions or scope limitations in the contract context support the existence of a confidentiality provision for the agreement or negotiations.
arguments.legal_rule: Contract interpretation relies on explicit definitions and scope; lack of supporting definitions weakens or attacks inferred obligations.
